Everything below runs in your browser, right here on this page, which is itself a
qmd-fast document. Each demo shows its **Result** and the real **Source** that
produced it: open the Source tab and you are reading the exact `.qmd` cell. No
screenshots, no video.

{{< include _includes/three-scene.qmd >}}

## A surface you can shape and spin

A parametric wave-interference mesh, rendered with WebGL. Drag to orbit, scroll to
zoom, and move the sliders to reshape it in real time. The renderer is transparent,
so it follows the page theme, and the whole thing is the `{js}` cell in the
**Source** tab, around forty lines of plain text.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Result

{{< input name="detail" type="slider" min="16" max="80" step="4" value="48" label="detail" >}}
{{< input name="twist" type="slider" min="0" max="6" step="0.2" value="2" label="twist" >}}
{{< input name="amplitude" type="slider" min="0" max="1.4" step="0.05" value="0.7" label="amplitude" >}}

```{js}
//| echo: false
const makeScene3D = qmd.get("makeScene3D");
const reduce = matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches;
const host = document.createElement("div");
host.style.minHeight = "460px";

const build = async () => {
  let el;
  try {
    let S = null, mesh = null, lastN = -1, lastT = NaN, lastA = NaN;
    el = await makeScene3D((scene, THREE) => {
      S = { scene, THREE };
      const key = new THREE.DirectionalLight(0xffffff, 1.1);
      key.position.set(4, 6, 5);
      scene.add(key);
    }, invalidation, {
      width: 640, height: 460, alpha: true, cameraPos: [0, 5.5, 7.5],
      ambientIntensity: 0.9, autoRotate: !reduce, minDistance: 4, maxDistance: 14,
      onFrame: () => {
        if (!S) return;
        const n = Math.round(qmd.value("detail") ?? 48);
        const twist = +(qmd.value("twist") ?? 2);
        const amp = +(qmd.value("amplitude") ?? 0.7);
        if (n !== lastN) {
          lastN = n; lastT = NaN;
          if (mesh) { S.scene.remove(mesh); mesh.geometry.dispose(); mesh.material.dispose(); }
          const geo = new S.THREE.PlaneGeometry(6, 6, n, n);
          mesh = new S.THREE.Mesh(geo, new S.THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({
            color: 0x4c8dff, metalness: 0.12, roughness: 0.5, side: S.THREE.DoubleSide,
          }));
          mesh.rotation.x = -Math.PI / 2.3;
          S.scene.add(mesh);
        }
        if (twist !== lastT || amp !== lastA) {
          lastT = twist; lastA = amp;
          const p = mesh.geometry.attributes.position;
          for (let i = 0; i < p.count; i++) {
            const x = p.getX(i), y = p.getY(i), r = Math.hypot(x, y);
            p.setZ(i, amp * Math.sin(r * twist) * Math.cos(x * 0.9));
          }
          p.needsUpdate = true;
          mesh.geometry.computeVertexNormals();
        }
      },
    });
  } catch (e) {
    el = document.createElement("p");
    el.className = "qmd-muted";
    el.textContent = "The 3D preview needs network access to load Three.js from esm.sh.";
  }
  host.replaceChildren(el);
};

if (reduce) build();
else {
  const io = new IntersectionObserver((es, o) => {
    if (es[0].isIntersecting) { o.disconnect(); build(); }
  });
  io.observe(host);
  invalidation.then(() => io.disconnect());
}
return host;
```

      onFrame: () => {

        const n = Math.round(qmd.value("detail") ?? 48);
        const twist = +(qmd.value("twist") ?? 2);
        const amp = +(qmd.value("amplitude") ?? 0.7);
        if (n !== lastN) {
          lastN = n; lastT = NaN;
          if (mesh) { S.scene.remove(mesh); mesh.geometry.dispose(); mesh.material.dispose(); }
          const geo = new S.THREE.PlaneGeometry(6, 6, n, n);
          mesh = new S.THREE.Mesh(geo, new S.THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({
            color: 0x4c8dff, metalness: 0.12, roughness: 0.5, side: S.THREE.DoubleSide,
          }));

          S.scene.add(mesh);
        }

          lastT = twist; lastA = amp;
          const p = mesh.geometry.attributes.position;
          for (let i = 0; i < p.count; i++) {
            const x = p.getX(i), y = p.getY(i), r = Math.hypot(x, y);
            p.setZ(i, amp * Math.sin(r * twist) * Math.cos(x * 0.9));
          }
          p.needsUpdate = true;
          mesh.geometry.computeVertexNormals();
        }
      },
    });
  } catch (e) {
    el = document.createElement("p");
    el.className = "qmd-muted";
    el.textContent = "The 3D preview needs network access to load Three.js from esm.sh.";

  host.replaceChildren(el);
};

if (reduce) build();
else {
  const io = new IntersectionObserver((es, o) => {

## One source, watched as you scroll

Scroll the narration; the stage tracks the step in view. The active step sets a
reactive value (`stage`), so the sticky `{js}` cell re-runs as you scroll. The whole
`.scrolly` skeleton is in the **Source** tab.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Result

::: {.scrolly name="stage"}
```{js}
//| input: stage
//| echo: false
const stage = qmd.value("stage") || "one-source";
const wrap = document.createElement("div");
wrap.style.cssText = "min-height:300px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:16px;align-items:center;justify-content:center";
const tile = (t, hi) => {
  const d = document.createElement("div");
  d.textContent = t;
  d.style.cssText = "padding:12px 18px;border-radius:8px;font:600 14px/1.2 var(--qmd-font-head);text-align:center;min-width:170px;"
    + (hi ? "border:1px solid var(--qmd-accent);background:var(--qmd-accent);color:#fff"
          : "border:1px solid var(--qmd-border);background:var(--qmd-code-bg);color:var(--qmd-fg)");
  return d;
};
const group = (dir, ...k) => { const g = document.createElement("div"); g.style.cssText = `display:flex;flex-direction:${dir};gap:12px;flex-wrap:wrap;justify-content:center`; k.forEach(x => g.append(x)); return g; };
const note = (t) => { const p = document.createElement("p"); p.textContent = t; p.style.cssText = "margin:0;max-width:30rem;text-align:center;color:var(--qmd-muted)"; return p; };
const views = {
  "one-source": () => [tile("post.qmd"), note("One plain-text file: prose, math, and code cells.")],
  "blocks": () => [group("column", tile("# heading"), tile("paragraph"), tile("{python} cell"), tile("figure (output)")), note("Parsed into top-level blocks, each with a content-hash id.")],
  "diff": () => [group("column", tile("# heading"), tile("paragraph"), tile("{python} cell", true), tile("figure (output)", true)), note("Edit one cell: only that block and its output re-render. Scroll, canvas, and kernel survive.")],
  "many-outputs": () => [group("row", tile("blog post"), tile("slide deck"), tile("book")), note("The same blocks become a post, a deck, or a book.")],
};
(views[stage] || views["one-source"])().forEach(n => wrap.append(n));
return wrap;
```
::: {.step state="one-source"}
**One `.qmd` file.** Plain text: prose, math, and executable code cells, together in one place.
:::
::: {.step state="blocks"}
**Parsed into blocks.** Each top-level element becomes a block with a content-hash id and a source position, so the system can follow it across edits.
:::
::: {.step state="diff"}
**A save diffs only what changed.** Edit one cell and only that block, plus its output, crosses the wire. Your scroll, your live canvas, and your warm kernel all survive.
:::
::: {.step state="many-outputs"}
**One source, many outputs.** The same blocks render as a blog post, a slide deck, or a multi-chapter book. Choose the output in the front matter.
:::
:::

## A live equation and its plot

The square wave is a sum of odd harmonics. Drag $N$ and watch the partial sum
sharpen toward the square. The equation is rendered offline by KaTeX, the chart by
the vendored Observable Plot, and both react to the same slider:

$$ f(t)=\sum_{k=1}^{N}\frac{\sin\!\big((2k-1)\,2\pi t\big)}{2k-1}. $$

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Result

{{< input name="harmonics" type="slider" min="1" max="24" step="1" value="5" label="N (harmonics)" >}}

```{js}
//| input: harmonics
//| echo: false
const N = qmd.value("harmonics");
const ys = Array.from({ length: 500 }, (_, t) =>
  d3.range(1, N + 1).reduce((s, k) => s + Math.sin(2 * Math.PI * (2 * k - 1) * t / 500) / (2 * k - 1), 0));
return Plot.lineY(ys, { curve: "basis", stroke: "#4c8dff" })
  .plot({ height: 240, marginLeft: 40, x: { label: "t" }, y: { label: "amplitude" } });
```

### Source
